Looking at this question, I need to consider which microcin homolog has been identified across all known E. coli phylogroups (A, B1, B2, D, and others).

Microcins are small antimicrobial peptides produced by E. coli. The microcin C family (which includes Microcin E492, Microcin H47, and Microcin I47) encodes ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides.

Among the options, Microcin E492 (encoded by the mccE operon) is the most widely distributed microcin in E. coli. Genomic studies have shown that homologs of the microcin E492/microcin C family genes are present across all major E. coli phylogroups, making it the most universally conserved microcin system in this species.

[ANSWER]F[/ANSWER]
